info.title: rpc.aex402.com
info.description: Multi-chain RPC proxy (Solana + EVM chains) + OpenAI-compatible AI proxy with x402 micropayments. Full docs: https://rpc.aex402.com/llms.txt
info.x-guidance:
This API provides multi-chain JSON-RPC proxying (Solana + EVM chains) and OpenAI-compatible AI chat completions, both payable via x402 micropayments on Solana.

**Getting started:**
1. Free tier: 10 requests/minute per IP, no auth needed. Response header X-Rate-Remaining shows calls left this minute. Heavier use is pay-per-call via x402 ($0.01 buys 100 calls).
2. When the free tier is exceeded, the server returns HTTP 402 with full payment instructions in the body (schema: PaymentRequired402).
3. ZERO-QUOTA DISCOVERY (two ways): (a) GET /.well-known/x402 — paymentRequirements field carries payTo, token mints, and atomic amounts; (b) POST / with header "Prefer: x402-probe" (any body) returns the full 402 payment instructions. Neither consumes quota.
4. Pay with USDC, USDT, SOL, or $ANSEM on Solana mainnet. Minimum payment: $0.01 = 100 credits. The 402 body's paidTier.accepts[] lists exact mint addresses and atomic amounts; paidTier.payTo is the recipient.
5. Two ways to settle: (a) build+sign a Solana transfer TX, base64-encode it, and retry the request with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header (the worker co-signs as fee payer and submits — you pay no gas); or (b) send tokens to payTo yourself, then claim with GET /topup?sig=<tx_signature>.
6. Success responses include headers: X-Session (HMAC session token, 24h sliding TTL), X-Credits-Remaining, PAYMENT-RESPONSE (settlement JSON). Use X-Session on subsequent requests.
7. For long-lived programmatic access, create an API key via POST /v1/api-keys (requires Ed25519 wallet signature) and use Authorization: Bearer sk-aex-v1-*. Header-less tooling (forge/hardhat/MetaMask/web3.js, which speak raw JSON-RPC and can't set headers) can instead embed the credential in the URL query — ?key=sk-aex-v1-* or ?session=ses-* on any endpoint (e.g. https://rpc.aex402.com/rh?key=sk-aex-v1-...), identical to the header and drawing from prepaid credits rather than the free per-IP rate limit.

**Key endpoints:**
- POST / — Solana JSON-RPC proxy; eth_* methods auto-route to Robinhood Chain (1 credit per call)
- POST /rh — Robinhood Chain mainnet (EVM, chain ID 4663); /rh/testnet for testnet (46630)
- POST /hl — HyperEVM (EVM, chain ID 999)
- POST /eth — Ethereum Mainnet (EVM, chain ID 1)
- POST /base — Base Mainnet (EVM, chain ID 8453)
- POST /stable — Stable Mainnet (EVM, chain ID 988, USDT0 gas)
- POST /plasma — Plasma Mainnet (EVM, chain ID 9745)
- POST /tempo — Tempo Mainnet Presto (EVM, chain ID 4217)
- POST /codex — Codex Mainnet (EVM, chain ID 81224)
- POST /v1/chat/completions — OpenAI-compatible AI chat (1-50 credits depending on model/tokens)
- GET /credits?wallet=<pubkey> — Check credit balance (free)
- GET /health — Backend status (free)
- POST /mcp — MCP server: any Solana/EVM RPC method (solana_rpc/evm_rpc), all read endpoints (api_get), AMM tools, TX builders, and mcp_linq for one-call fan-out + fluent LINQ-style aggregation

**Pricing:** 1 credit = $0.0001. RPC calls cost 1 credit. AI calls cost 1-50 credits based on token usage.

post.description: 32 primary tools. Generic: solana_rpc (any Solana/Slonana method), evm_rpc (any EVM method — Robinhood, HyperEVM, Ethereum, Base, Stable, Plasma, Tempo, Codex), hl_info (Hyperliquid perps/spot order-book data), api_get (any public GET endpoint), mcp_linq (one read-only call with cross-chain fan-out, reducers, JSON pipeline, or LINQ-like fluent method chains such as results.selectMany(...).where(...).groupBy(...).take(...)). Discovery: discover_programs (curated + auto-discovered programs/contracts across all chains + hourly token census where available), describe_program (introspect any address — Solana executable/owner, EVM contract/ERC-20 + Blockscout enrichment where available), search_tokens (query the Robinhood/HyperEVM token+NFT census by symbol/name — holders, market cap, live price), discovery_health (freshness/failures of the discovery cron), reconstruct_abi (rebuild a PARTIAL interface from resolved bytecode selectors + event topics — novel selectors stay unresolved). Typed Solana: solana_getBalance, solana_getAccountInfo, solana_getTokenAccountsByOwner, solana_getTransaction, solana_getLatestBlockhash, solana_getSignaturesForAddress, solana_sendTransaction, solana_getSlot, solana_buildTransfer. AMM: aex402_listPools, aex402_getPool, aex402_quote, aex402_buildSwap. Bridge: bridge_quote (cross-chain bridge/swap via LI.FI/Jumper — any chain incl. Robinhood 4663, returns an unsigned tx), bridge_status. AI: ai_chat, agent_delegate. Call tools/list for input schemas.

BearerAuth.description: API key (sk-aex-v1-...). Recommended for programmatic access. Create via POST /v1/api-keys.

ApiKeyQuery.name: key
ApiKeyQuery.description: Same API key (sk-aex-v1-...) passed in the URL query (?key=...) instead of the Authorization header — for header-less tooling (forge, hardhat, MetaMask, web3.js). Identical effect to BearerAuth; draws from prepaid credits, not the free rate limit. A ?session=ses-... query is likewise accepted in place of X-Session.

SessionHeader.name: X-Session
SessionHeader.description: HMAC session token (ses-...). Issued in the X-Session response header after x402 settlement (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE) or GET /topup?sig=. Proves wallet ownership. 24h sliding TTL — every credit-spending response returns a refreshed token.

WalletHeader.name: X-Wallet
WalletHeader.description: Solana wallet pubkey. READ-ONLY without session/key (balance check only).

PaymentSignature.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
PaymentSignature.description: Inline x402 settlement: base64-encoded signed Solana transfer transaction paying >= the amount from the 402 body (paidTier.accepts[]) to paidTier.payTo. The worker verifies (3-6 instructions, CU limit <= 5000, recipient must match payTo), co-signs as fee payer, simulates, submits, and allocates credits — the payer never spends gas. Success returns PAYMENT-RESPONSE + X-Session + X-Credits-Remaining headers.

PaymentRequired402.description: Body of every HTTP 402 response. Contains everything needed to construct payment. Elicit without burning quota: POST / with body {}.

accepts.description: Accepted assets with exact atomic amounts

mint.description: SPL mint address (base58); SOL uses the wrapped SOL mint sentinel

amount.description: Minimum payment in atomic units of this asset (USDC/USDT: 6 decimals, SOL: 9/lamports)

payTo.description: Merchant recipient address — the transfer destination

feePayer.description: Facilitator fee-payer address (must NOT appear in your instruction accounts)

facilitator.description: External facilitator base URL (alternative to inline PAYMENT-SIGNATURE)

quickstart.description: Copy-paste onboarding steps incl. /topup and API key flow

message.description: Signed message: "Sign to generate API key for rpc.aex402.com\nTimestamp: <unix>\nWallet: <pubkey>"

solAmount.description: SOL to spend (buy) / notional (sell). Per-trade capped at 0.02 SOL; omit for the agent default.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional client-supplied key. A repeat call with the same key returns the original result WITHOUT re-executing or re-charging (replayed:true).

ok.description: true when the trade confirmed on-chain

sig.description: Confirmed transaction signature (base58), or null if it did not confirm

replayed.description: true if this was an idempotent replay (original fee already charged)

feeCredits.description: 100 on a fresh confirmed fill; 0 on replay or no-confirm

remaining.description: Owner credit balance after the debit (present only when a fee was charged)

note.description: Explanation when feeCredits is 0 (replay vs. no-confirm)

x-mcp-tools.name: aex402_rh_pool
x-mcp-tools.description: Get the live state of the aeX402 AMM on Robinhood Chain (EVM 4663) — the diamond-contract port of the Solana AMM. The AMM is the set of GRADUATED launchpad coins whose pools are seeded in-diamond on the canonical launchpad (0xED2F); this enumerates them live by scanning VPoolGraduated events + reading each pool's reserves, so it tracks reality as coins graduate. Returns graduatedPools[] (poolId, token, reserves, TVL), graduatedPoolCount, and status ("live" | "no-graduated-pools" | "unknown"), plus the legacy standalone 0xA1F6 USDG/WETH pool (legacy-drained). Distinct from the chain's Uniswap-fork DEX. No inputs.

x-mcp-tools.name: launch_token
x-mcp-tools.description: Launch a memecoin on the aeX402 launchpad on Robinhood Chain (EVM 4663) for a FIXED pump.fun-style bonding curve (1B supply, starts 0.0001 USDG, graduates at 10,000 USDG raised, quoted in USDG). You supply only identity — name + ticker (+ optional description/image/links). DEFAULT (custodial): the aeX402 backend SIGNS + SUBMITS the createVPool tx for you, so a claude.ai user with NO WALLET can launch in one call; returns {ok,status,txHash,vpId}. Optionally pass `creator` (a 0x address) to record as the coin owner. Pass build:true instead to get an UNSIGNED tx {to,value,data} to submit yourself (non-custodial — that requires `creator` and makes you the on-chain creator). A custodial call SIMULATES first, so a failure burns no gas: status "gated" means createVPool reverts in simulation (cause not determined — likeliest are the ticker still being claimed by a bonding coin or this vpId being taken; see `detail`/`revertData`), and status "unreachable" means the chain could not be reached, which is retryable. The launchpad is NOT chain-gated: createVPool simulates clean from an arbitrary sender (measured 2026-09-25).

creator.description: OPTIONAL 0x EVM address recorded as the coin owner (and seeds the vpId). REQUIRED only when build:true (then it is the self-signing on-chain creator).

image.description: Image URL (https:// or ipfs:// only) — off-chain metadata

pad.description: OPTIONAL aeX402 launchpad slug the coin is launched on. Its vpId then starts with that pad's tag, so the pad lists it. Applies on BOTH the custodial (default) and build:true paths

build.description: If true, return an UNSIGNED tx to submit yourself (non-custodial) instead of the backend launching for you. Default false.

ok.description: Custodial mode: whether the launch was submitted

status.description: submitted | gated | custodial-disabled | exists | rate-limited | insufficient-gas | submit-failed

txHash.description: Custodial mode: the createVPool tx hash

data.description: build mode: createVPool calldata to submit

metadata.description: Off-chain metadata (stored server-side in custodial mode)

x-mcp-tools.name: solana_rpc
x-mcp-tools.description: Call ANY Solana-compatible JSON-RPC method by name — full RPC surface beyond the typed solana_* tools (getProgramAccounts, getBlock, getEpochInfo, simulateTransaction, ...). Defaults to Solana mainnet; pass network:slonana to query Slonana (rpc.slonana.com), which additionally exposes RPC methods no other network has: getAlpenglowHealth (consensus migration status), getBridgeStatus, getAexchanRelays, getValidatorStats, quote. (listSvmNetworks/enableSvmNetwork/disableSvmNetwork/setNetworkRpcUrl also exist but are inert API-compat stubs — listSvmNetworks always reports one hardcoded network and the enable/disable/set calls ignore their arguments and return true; verified in source, not live network-management controls.) For tools that exist ONLY on Slonana's MCP server with no RPC-method equivalent (the aea_* agent registry), use mcp_call instead.

method.description: Solana RPC method name, e.g. getEpochInfo

params.description: Positional params array (method-specific). Omit for no params.

x-mcp-tools.name: mcp_call

Known servers: slonana. Call that server's tools/list first if you don't know its tool names.

server.description: Federated server name. One of: slonana

tool.description: Tool name on that server, e.g. aea_list_services. Omit both tool and arguments to list that server's tools instead.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool call, per that server's own schema.

x-mcp-tools.name: evm_rpc
x-mcp-tools.description: Call ANY EVM JSON-RPC method on a supported chain — eth_getBalance, eth_call, eth_blockNumber, eth_sendRawTransaction, eth_getLogs, ... Chains: robinhood (4663) / robinhood-testnet (46630), hyperevm (999), ethereum (1), base (8453), stable (988), plasma (9745), tempo (4217), codex (81224), arc (5042, Circle mainnet).

method.description: EVM RPC method name, e.g. eth_getBalance

params.description: Positional params array (method-specific). Omit for no params.

network.description: Chain slug: robinhood (default; legacy mainnet alias accepted), robinhood-testnet, hyperevm, ethereum/eth, base, stable/tether, plasma, tempo, codex, or arc (Circle mainnet)

x-mcp-tools.name: mcp_linq
x-mcp-tools.description: Primary LINQ-style MCP workflow tool. Run one bounded MCP call: fan out up to 32 READ-ONLY tool calls across chains, then compose the combined result with fluent chains like results.selectMany(...).where(...).groupBy(...).orderByDesc(...).take(...), JSON pipeline steps, or reducers. Use mcp_linq when you want one aggregate answer instead of N tool calls.

calls.description: Read-only MCP tool calls to run. Each call has {id?, tool, args?, pick?}. pick is a dot path into that call output; [] flattens arrays.

id.description: Stable label for this subcall; defaults to tool:index.

tool.description: Read-only tool name, e.g. evm_rpc, solana_rpc, discover_programs, search_tokens, hl_info.

pick.description: Optional dot path to return from this subcall, e.g. count or programs[].activity.

path.description: Dot path into the batch result, e.g. results[].picked or results[].output.programs[].activity.

by.description: For group* reducers: dot path inside each selected item used as the group key.

value.description: For groupSum/groupAvg: numeric path inside each selected item. Defaults to the item itself.

sortBy.description: For top: numeric/string path inside each selected item used for ordering.

limit.description: Max rows returned by top/concat/group reducers (default 10, max 100).

reduce.description: Named reductions to compute from subcall outputs. Example: {"total":{"op":"sum","path":"results[].picked"},"top":{"op":"top","path":"results[]","sortBy":"picked","limit":5}}.

pipeline.description: LINQ-style chained transforms over the raw batch result. Each step feeds the next. Ops: from, expand, where, select/project, groupBy, orderBy/sort, take/limit, skip, distinct, count, sum, avg, min, max, first, top. Example: [{"op":"from","path":"results[]"},{"op":"expand","path":"output.programs[]"},{"op":"where","path":"type","in":["token","canonical-token"]},{"op":"groupBy","by":"_chain","as":"chain","aggregates":{"tokens":{"op":"count"},"activity":{"op":"sum","path":"activity"}}},{"op":"orderBy","path":"tokens","dir":"desc"},{"op":"take","count":5}].

op.description: from | expand | where | select | project | groupBy | orderBy | sort | take | limit | skip | distinct | count | sum | avg | min | max | first | top

path.description: Dot path. [] flattens arrays. "$" or "." means the current item.

fields.description: Projection map: outputField -> input path. Use {"literal":value} for literal strings.

aggregates.description: groupBy aggregates: name -> {op,path?}; ops: count, sum, avg, min, max, first, top.

linq.description: LINQ-like query string compiled into pipeline steps. Supports fluent dot chaining and query clauses. .where()/.map()/.select() bodies AND .orderBy()/.orderByDesc()/.distinctBy()/.groupBy() keys are all real expressions — ternaries, &&/||, comparisons, arithmetic, member/index access, object/array literals, and a small method whitelist (.includes/.startsWith/.endsWith/.toLowerCase/.toUpperCase/.trim/.slice/.indexOf/.split/.join, Math.min/max/round/floor/ceil/abs, String()/Number()/Boolean()) all work, e.g. results.map(r => r.ok ? ({chain: r.id, height: r.output}) : ({chain: r.id, height: -1})), or ranking by a COMPUTED score: results.where(r => r.ok).orderByDesc(r => r.output.volume24h * r.output.priceChangePct).take(10) — the ranking key is not limited to a bare field. Fluent example: results.selectMany(r => r.output.programs[]).where(p => p.type in ("token","canonical-token")).groupBy(p => p._chain, assets=count(), activity=sum(activity)).orderByDesc(assets).take(5). Clause example: from results[] | expand output.programs[] | where type in ("token","canonical-token") | group by _chain as chain select assets=count(), activity=sum(activity) | order by assets desc | take 5.

ignoreFailures.description: When reduce/pipeline/linq is used, a failed subcall is normally still reported in `failures` alongside the aggregate result, since a `.where(ok)`-style query would otherwise make it invisible. Set true to suppress that and get back only {reductions?, result?} — use when you already expect some chains/calls to fail and only want whatever succeeded. Defaults to false (failures still shown) because silently dropping an error is a real information loss, not just an efficiency choice — this one is opt-in on purpose.

ok.description: omitted when reduce/pipeline/linq was requested — the aggregation response is just the answer, not this batch-fanout shape

calls.description: number of subcalls attempted; omitted when reduce/pipeline/linq was requested

items.description: per-call result: id, tool, ok, picked/output or error

results.description: omitted when reduce/pipeline/linq was requested — see failures instead for what went wrong

reductions.description: named reducer outputs; omitted when args.reduce was not passed

result.description: The pipeline/linq output value — the entire point of the call when args.pipeline or args.linq was passed, returned alone rather than wrapped; omitted when neither was passed

failures.description: omitted when every subcall succeeded, when ignoreFailures:true was passed, or when no aggregation was requested (failures show inside results instead)

x-mcp-tools.name: bridge_quote
x-mcp-tools.description: Bridge/swap ANY asset across ANY chain via LI.FI (the engine behind Jumper) — e.g. Arbitrum USDC → Robinhood Chain (4663) USDG, or bridge into ETH for gas. Returns the best route (estimated output, fees, bridge used, duration) PLUS an unsigned transactionRequest (to/data/value/gasLimit) that the CALLER signs and submits on the fromChain — no keys are held here. Chains by id or key (1 Ethereum, 42161 Arbitrum, 8453 Base, 10 Optimism, 137 Polygon, 999 HyperEVM, 4663 Robinhood Chain). Tokens by symbol or 0x address.

fromChain.description: Source chain id or key, e.g. 42161 or ARB

toChain.description: Destination chain id or key, e.g. 4663 (Robinhood Chain)

fromToken.description: Source token symbol or 0x address, e.g. USDC

toToken.description: Destination token symbol or 0x address, e.g. USDG or ETH

fromAmount.description: Amount in the source token's smallest unit (e.g. 1000000 = 1 USDC at 6 decimals)

fromAddress.description: Sender 0x address on the source chain

toAddress.description: Recipient on the destination chain (defaults to fromAddress)

transactionRequest.description: UNSIGNED tx (to, data, value, gasLimit) — caller signs & submits on the fromChain

x-mcp-tools.name: bridge_status
x-mcp-tools.description: Track a cross-chain bridge submitted via bridge_quote — returns DONE / PENDING / FAILED plus the receiving-chain tx once it completes. Pass the source-chain tx hash (and the bridge tool from the quote for a faster lookup).

txHash.description: Source-chain transaction hash from submitting the bridge tx

bridge.description: The bridge tool from bridge_quote (e.g. across, stargate) — optional

x-mcp-tools.name: hl_info
x-mcp-tools.description: Query the Hyperliquid Info API — the perps/spot order-book data layer (read-only, no auth). The 'type' field selects the query: meta (perps universe + leverage), l2Book (order book for a coin), allMids (mid prices), clearinghouseState (a user's positions/margin), spotMeta, meta+assetCtxs (mark/funding/OI), candleSnapshot, and more. For type:metaAndAssetCtxs specifically: the raw response is TWO PARALLEL top-level arrays (universe names, asset contexts) correlated only by array position — do not try to read/scan it directly for '200+ coins' style questions (funding-rate outliers, biggest open interest, highest volume). Pass rankBy instead: it joins the two arrays server-side, sorts, and returns only the top N — the correct way to answer 'what has the highest/most extreme funding/OI/volume right now'.

type.description: Info request type, e.g. meta, l2Book, allMids, clearinghouseState, metaAndAssetCtxs

coin.description: Coin symbol for l2Book/candleSnapshot (e.g. BTC, ETH)

user.description: 0x address for user-scoped queries (clearinghouseState, openOrders, userFills)

rankBy.description: type:metaAndAssetCtxs ONLY. One of funding | fundingAbs | openInterest | volume. Joins each coin's name to its funding/OI/volume, drops delisted coins, sorts, and returns {ranked, rankBy, dir, totalCoins} instead of the raw two-array response. Use fundingAbs for "biggest funding outlier either direction" (ranks by |funding|); use funding for "most positive/most negative" specifically (with dir).

limit.description: rankBy only: how many ranked rows to return (default 20, max 100)

dir.description: rankBy only: asc | desc (default desc — highest rankBy value first)

startTime.description: candleSnapshot only: start time epoch ms (default: endTime minus 500 intervals)

endTime.description: candleSnapshot only: end time epoch ms (default: now)

x-mcp-tools.name: api_get
x-mcp-tools.description: GET any public read endpoint of rpc.aex402.com: /health, /credits?wallet=, /pumpfun?limit=, /pumpfun/tuple?mint=, /security/<pool>, /market/list, /sniper/leaderboard, /sniper/bets?id=, /settlement/<sig>, /settlements/<wallet>, /ai/models, /ai/stats, /leaderboard, /openapi.json, /llms.txt, /rh/pools (Robinhood), /hl/pools (HyperEVM), /base/pools (Base Uniswap v3), /eth/pools (Ethereum Uniswap v3), /arb/pools (Arbitrum Uniswap v3)

path.description: Endpoint path including query string, e.g. /security/9Wq.. or /pumpfun?limit=5

x-mcp-tools.name: discover_programs
x-mcp-tools.description: Discover on-chain programs/contracts across every chain this RPC supports (Solana, Slonana SVM, Robinhood, HyperEVM, Ethereum, Base, Stable, Plasma, Tempo, Codex). Returns a curated seed MERGED with programs/contracts AUTO-DISCOVERED from recent block activity (refreshed hourly) — each carries an `activity` count of recent invocations/calls; entries with type "discovered" were seen live on-chain but not yet named. Use this to learn what is actually active on-chain right now, then describe_program to introspect any specific address.

chain.description: Filter to one chain: solana | slonana | robinhood | hyperevm | ethereum | base | stable | plasma | tempo | codex. Omit or "all" for every chain.

coverage.description: what this scan enumerated: a string on the single-chain response, the full per-chain map on the all-chains response

note.description: caveats about what this scan did and did not see

programs.description: array on the single-chain response; a per-chain {chain: program[]} map on the all-chains response

x-mcp-tools.name: describe_program
x-mcp-tools.description: Introspect ANY specific program/contract address on a chain. Solana/Slonana: returns executable, owner, data size, and whether it is a known program. EVM: RPC-verified facts (is-contract, code size, ERC-20 name/symbol/decimals, EIP-1967 proxy → implementation) PLUS Blockscout explorer enrichment when available.

chain.description: solana | slonana | robinhood | hyperevm | ethereum | base | stable | plasma | tempo | codex

address.description: Program id (base58, Solana/Slonana) or contract address (0x…, EVM)

exists.description: Solana/Slonana only — omitted when the chain is EVM (isContract is the EVM equivalent)

isProgram.description: Solana/Slonana only — omitted when the chain is EVM

executable.description: Solana/Slonana only — omitted when the chain is EVM

owner.description: owning program. Solana/Slonana only — omitted when the chain is EVM

dataLen.description: account data length in bytes. Solana/Slonana only — omitted when the chain is EVM (codeSize is the EVM equivalent)

lamports.description: Solana/Slonana only — omitted when the chain is EVM

isContract.description: EVM only — omitted when the chain is Solana/Slonana, where executable/isProgram carry this instead

codeSize.description: EVM bytecode length in bytes. EVM only — omitted when the chain is Solana/Slonana (dataLen is the Solana equivalent)

erc20.description: ERC-20 name/symbol/decimals. EVM only — omitted when the address is not an ERC-20, or the chain is Solana/Slonana

proxy.description: EIP-1967 proxy standard + implementation. EVM only — omitted when the address is not a proxy, or the chain is Solana/Slonana

known.description: curated registry entry {id,name,type,note} when the address is recognised

x-mcp-tools.name: reconstruct_abi
x-mcp-tools.description: Reconstruct a PARTIAL function/event interface for an EVM contract on a supported EVM chain from its BYTECODE — no source or verification needed. Extracts PUSH4 function selectors + recent event topic0 hashes and resolves the ones public signature DBs (openchain/4byte) know to human signatures. Works on UNVERIFIED contracts because bytecode is ground truth, but it is NOT a full ABI: novel/proprietary selectors DBs have never seen stay unresolved (decompile for those). Use it to understand what an unknown contract does before trusting behavior-based guesses.

chain.description: robinhood | hyperevm | ethereum | base | stable | plasma | tempo | codex

address.description: EVM contract address (0x…). For a proxy, pass the implementation for the real logic.

note.description: what the reconstruction could and could not resolve

x-mcp-tools.name: search_tokens
x-mcp-tools.description: Search the live token/NFT census for Robinhood Chain (4663) and HyperEVM (999) by symbol or name. Returns matching tokens with address, standard (erc20/erc721/erc1155), decimals, holders, market cap, and — for HyperEVM canonical tokens — live spot price + 24h volume. The census is refreshed hourly (canonical tokens from Hyperliquid spotMeta, top tokens from Blockscout, spam-filtered). Use this instead of discover_programs when you want a specific asset (e.g. "USDC on hyperevm", "stablecoins on robinhood") rather than the whole list.

query.description: Symbol or name substring, case-insensitive (e.g. "usdc", "hype"). Omit to list the top of the census.

chain.description: robinhood | hyperevm. Omit to search both.

censusAgeMin.description: minutes since the census cron last ran

items.description: address, symbol, name, standard, decimals, holders, marketCap, price

x-mcp-tools.name: discovery_health
x-mcp-tools.description: Report the freshness and health of the cross-chain program/token discovery pipeline: when the hourly cron last ran, how many programs/tokens each chain scan produced, and which scans failed. Use this to check whether discover_programs / search_tokens data is current before relying on it.

counts.description: per-chain program counts from the last scan
per-chain program count at that run

history.description: per-chain counts over the last <=24 cron runs, oldest first

failedScans.description: chains whose last scan errored (omitted when none)

emptyScans.description: chains whose last scan returned zero (omitted when none)

sourceErrors.description: per-chain list of what each live source ACTUALLY answered when it failed, e.g. "robinhood/ERC-20: blockscout /api/v2/tokens → 403". Says WHY a census is thin where seedsOnlyScans only says THAT it is. Capped at 4 entries per chain; when more were recorded the list carries a final "… +N more (T total)" string, so the count survives the truncation rather than the list silently reading as complete. Omitted when every source succeeded

seedsOnlyScans.description: chains whose last scan returned ONLY hardcoded canonical seeds — every live source returned nothing while the fallback held, so the count is non-zero and emptyScans does NOT list them. Sets status=degraded. Omitted when none

censusLiveRecords.description: per-census count of records the LIVE source returned, before any merge, cap or spam filter — the evidence behind seedsOnlyScans. 0 means the live source supplied nothing (the census is its fallback); -1 means this census was last written by a build that did not record the field, which is NOT the same as zero. Published even when healthy, so a reader can distinguish "source is fine" from "nothing was measured" without inferring it from a verdict. Never omitted: built over the census keys in counts, so every census always carries a value and -1 covers the pre-field case — the earlier exemption for records predating the field was retired when the conditional spread was removed

censusRecordsBeforeCap.description: per-census record count BEFORE the fungible (170) and NFT (50) caps. A count sitting exactly on its cap cannot say whether it is a finding or a ceiling — hyperevm_census reads 170 because 170 IS the cap. Compare against counts: a value here greater than the published count means that census was TRUNCATED, equal means it was not. -1 means the build that last wrote this census did not record the field. Never omitted, same construction as censusLiveRecords

x-mcp-tools.name: payment_help
x-mcp-tools.description: How to pay for API access (x402 micropayments) — the complete self-serve guide for agents: current prices, every accepted asset/chain (USDC/USDT/SOL/ANSEM on Solana, ETH/USDG on Robinhood Chain, USDC/HYPE on HyperEVM), the merchant addresses, step-by-step topup → session-token → API-key flow, and how to attach credentials to MCP calls. This tool is FREE and NEVER rate-limited — call it when you hit a 402 / rate limit to convert into a paid session ($0.01 minimum buys 100 calls, no signup).

paidTier.description: Prices, accepted assets with mints/contracts + merchant addresses, howToPay steps

mcp.description: MCP-specific: which methods stay free, how to attach X-Session / Bearer key to MCP requests

note.description: one-line summary of the cheapest path to a paid session

x-mcp-tools.name: search
x-mcp-tools.description: Search the aeX402 universe by keyword: tokens (Robinhood Chain + HyperEVM census), known programs/contracts (Solana, Robinhood, HyperEVM, Slonana), and live AeX402 AMM pools. Returns a result list; pass a result id to the fetch tool for full detail. Use the specialist tools (search_tokens, discover_programs, aex402_listPools) when you already know the entity type.

query.description: Keyword: token symbol/name ("usdg"), program name ("pump.fun"), contract address, or pool address.

id.description: Opaque id for fetch: token:<chain>:<address> | program:<chain>:<address> | pool:<address>

x-mcp-tools.name: fetch
x-mcp-tools.description: Fetch the full document for one search result id (from the search tool). Accepts token:<chain>:<address>, program:<chain>:<address>, or pool:<address>. Returns the entity detail (on-chain state for pools, census entry for tokens, registry/introspection for programs) as a document.

id.description: A search result id, e.g. "pool:G5d3qFZq..." or "token:robinhood:0x5fc5..." or "program:solana:3AMM53..."
